scope: Independent symbolic mean-field event identities and finite-tree Sankoff score enumeration; not stochastic expectation closure, numerical integration, or a proof assistant development.
assumptions: Positive deme populations Y_i; nonnegative lineage classes and event rates.
Class row sums equal ancestral counts A_i, with factorized endpoint occupancy q_ic = H_ic/Y_i and p_i = A_i/Y_i.
For a probabilistic event interpretation also require A_i <= Y_i; polynomial identities do not require this bound.
A forward transmission i->j has rate F_ij. Two ancestral endpoints coalesce in parent deme i; child-only ancestry transfers j->i at F_ij*(1-p_i)*q_jc.
Physical migration i->j has rate G_ij and backward class transfer j->i at G_ij*q_jc; diagonal physical migration is ignored.
Sankoff edge costs are nonnegative directed integers or infinity with zero diagonal; root state is free with zero root cost.
Descendant masses use an additional factorized first-moment closure within each deme.

generated_csv.class_rule: For H and J claims, two classes 1 and 2 use irreversible 1->2 Camin-Sokal merging: mixed pair becomes class 1 and increments J by 1. Pure pairs retain class.
generated_csv.contract: An explicitly supplied CSV must exist, have exactly the declared columns, and contain all 37 unique legacy_1 through legacy_37 claims and all 16 unique independent_claims; duplicate claims are rejected. Every row must simplify expression-expected to zero. All identifier tokens (including beta and z1 through z37) are declared as symbols, not SymPy builtin functions. Recognized claim names are additionally compared with independent event-derived expressions. All eight legacy claims 15 through 22 are independently compared with directional event equations under corresponding class-row constraints. Other unknown names are reported as cross-generator checks only, not independently derived claims. A CSV containing self-comparisons alone cannot pass.
